reference_query_plan.central_topic: Estimation error of regression-based global average treatment effect (GATE) estimators under network interference, characterized as corner-exposure extrapolation bias versus variance, across interference mechanisms, graphs and designs.
comparators: Horvitz-Thompson / Hajek estimators under exposure mappings (Aronow & Samii)
graph cluster randomization and network exposure (Ugander et al.; Eckles et al.)
model-based regression adjustment with graph-based covariates (Han & Ugander)
staggered rollout and covariance-optimized designs for total treatment effect
core_methods: regression-adjusted GATE estimation (fit outcome model on assigned treatments/neighbor exposures, predict all-treated vs all-control)
linear-in-neighbor-exposure ridge regression baseline and ridge ensembles with extrapolation-aware model selection
parametric exposure-mapping library with BIC-gated switch from linear fallback
block/wild bootstrap confidence intervals with design resampling

queries.rationale: Run shows bias dominates when the functional form of interference is wrong; need literature on misspecified exposure mappings.

queries.rationale: HT and Hajek baselines were run; Aronow & Samii and variance-bound work are expected comparators.

queries.rationale: Design-side comparator for reducing interference bias; relevant to the design axis of the simulation.

queries.query: difference-in-means bias under interference randomized experiments SUTVA violation
queries.rationale: Naive difference-in-means baseline had rmse_rel ~0.62 versus 0.14-0.18 for regression estimators.

queries.rationale: Second variant adds design-weighted residual correction to a linear base, an AIPW/doubly-robust-style construction.

queries.query: staggered rollout design total treatment effect interference without network knowledge
queries.rationale: Alternative design/estimator family for GATE under low-order interference, named in starter literature.

queries.query: extrapolation all-treated all-control counterfactual positivity violation network exposure
queries.rationale: Central finding: error governed by extrapolation to rarely observed full-exposure corner under random designs.

queries.rationale: Public graph data context if Facebook100 graphs were used for evaluation; cite data provenance only.

result_driven_themes: extrapolation to the all-treated/all-control corner makes bias dominate error (bias_rel ~0.16-0.19 vs rmse ~0.18-0.23) for flexible models
correctly specified exposure functional form reduces error in nonlinear-interference cases (case 6: 0.71 -> 0.27) while some cases remain unresolved (case 8 ~0.45)
model selection by information criterion for exposure-response specification
